Map-O-Matic

A free cartography studio that runs in your browser. Style your data as a map, compose a print-ready layout, collect field data on phones, and gather your maps into an interactive atlas. Nothing is installed or uploaded.

Your projects

Where your work lives: projects and datasets are saved in this browser, on this computer — nothing is uploaded to a server. To carry your work between machines, use ☁ Sync to cloud in the top bar: point Map-O-Matic at a folder you already sync (OneDrive, Google Drive or Dropbox) and every project is written there as a file whenever it saves, so you can pick up on another computer. Sync needs Chrome or Edge. Either way, on a shared computer it's wise to also download a project file (card menu → Export) or a full project archive as a portable backup, and take it with you.

Quick start

Map-O-Matic has four modules, in the buttons at the top. Work is saved in this browser as you go, one project at a time (click the Map-O-Matic name for the project list).

🧭 Map Maker: build the map.

+ Add data takes GeoJSON, CSV or Excel with coordinates, zipped shapefiles, your data library, or online sources. Select a layer to style it (categories, graduated colour or size, dot density, heatmaps, hexbins, cartograms), filter it and label it. The ⋯ menu and Tools tab hold the attribute table, field calculator and spatial tools. The map can switch to a globe or one of 13 projections, and ⇆ compares two layers with a swipe divider.

▣ Map Composer: lay out the page.

Arrange the map with a title, legend, north arrow, scale bar, text and images, or start from a template. Maps arrive from Map Maker ready to use; a map image from other software can be added with Map Frame and its scale calibrated. View as checks colours for colour blindness and greyscale print.

📱 Field Mapper: collect data on phones.

Design a form, share it by link or QR code, and record points, lines and areas with photos and audio. Collected data come back to the laptop and become Map Maker layers.

📖 Atlas: a book of maps.

Gather live maps, layouts, images and text into an atlas with a cover and contents page, in one of five designs. It reads as a flip-book or a scrolling page, and exports as a web page or a PDF.

Send / Export ▾ (top right).

Send the current map to Map Composer or the Atlas, share a live link, or export files: layout PDF/PNG/SVG, an interactive web map, data layers, or a whole project archive.

Keeping your work.

Projects live only in this browser. ☁ Sync to cloud also saves them to a folder you already sync (OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox); otherwise export a project file now and then, and always on a shared computer. 📝 Process Log lists every step you took, ready for a report.

About.

Map-O-Matic was created by Jonathan Cinnamon. It is free and runs entirely in your browser: your data stay on your computer, and the only network requests are for basemaps and the online data sources you choose. The full user guide covers every tool.

Map-O-Matic is provided “as is”, without warranty of any kind. It is a teaching and research tool: check your results before relying on them, respect the terms of the data sources and basemaps you use, and remember that you are responsible for the data you load and the maps you create and publish.

Layout templates

Templates give you a conventional starting arrangement — everything stays editable, and double-clicking a placeholder fills it with the real element in that spot. Applying a template replaces the current page contents.

Classic portrait

Centred title, full-width map, legend and marginalia below. The standard single-map layout.

Landscape + side panel

Map fills the left ~70%; title, legend, north arrow, and notes stack in a right panel.

Two-frame comparison

Two map frames side by side under one title — for before/after or variable comparisons.

Set reference distance

Enter the real-world distance between the two points you clicked.

Fields

Export layer

GeoJSON exports are valid FeatureCollections and include any calculated fields. Note: Save project files are for reloading work in this tool and are not GeoJSON — use this export for other GIS software.

Spatial tools

Send map to Layout

The current map view will be captured as a high-resolution image and placed on the layout page, with the scale calibrated automatically from the map. Pan/zoom the map to the exact extent you want first.

Build an inset / locator map

Pan and zoom the basemap. Optionally add a data layer or draw a locator box. “Add to layout” captures a snapshot you can move and resize on the page.

Export

Margin guides and live-embed previews are excluded automatically. Live embeds print as placeholders — swap them for image frames before submitting.

Share this map

Your styled, interactive map is packed into a link — no upload, no account, nothing sent to a server. Anyone who opens the link sees the live map: pan, zoom and click. Paste the embed code into ArcGIS StoryMaps (an Embed block) or any web page.

View in browser ↗

Your interactive map is ready

The HTML file just downloaded is a complete, self-contained interactive map. Put it online, then embed it anywhere.

Drag the file you just downloaded onto the page; it goes live in under a minute.

Until you paste a published address, the code points at the file name — replace it with your real URL, or use step 2 to fill it in. Paste this into an ArcGIS StoryMaps Embed block or any web page.

Add data from online sources

Natural Earth — the standard public-domain base layers used in professional cartography.

Fetches live OpenStreetMap features inside the current Map Maker view — zoom to your study area first. Community-contributed data: coverage and quality vary.

Results are capped at 8,000 features per query. Complex multipolygon features may be omitted.

Search open-data portals for map layers. Opendatasoft portals, ArcGIS Hub sites (the open-data sites of many cities, regions and agencies) and public ArcGIS Online layers load straight into the map. Catalogues whose map services don't allow loading from a web page show download links instead.

Examples: a .geojson export link from any open data portal, or an Esri REST endpoint ending in /FeatureServer/0. The source must allow cross-origin access (most public portals do).

Add from data library

Datasets from all your projects. Tick every one you want, then Add selected — each becomes a new layer in the current project that references the shared dataset.

Add live embed (on-screen preview)

Paste an embed URL from a publicly shared web map (e.g. a map viewer's “Embed map” option). It displays live and interactive on screen, but exports as a placeholder — use an image map frame for the final version.

Place points from coordinates

UTM zones are 6° of longitude wide, numbered eastward from 180°W: zone = (longitude + 180) ÷ 6, rounded up. North or South marks the hemisphere. Check that the preview names the right area before loading.

Process log

Every data step recorded in this project, plus the current design settings. Copy it into your report and edit it into prose: it is a record of what you did, not a finished methods section.
